pl-l4d46c4-d1e115.summary: States that it is easy to find in Scripture works attributed to mercy, to justice, and to goodness.

pl-l4d46c4-d1e118.summary: Notes that for mercy and justice this is plain, while the difference of goodness and mercy is less evident.

pl-l4d46c4-d1e121.summary: Cites Augustine: works that free some from misery pertain properly to mercy; to goodness belong not only these but the making and governing of natural things; to mercy it belongs to cleanse from sins and free from misery, to goodness to have created heaven and earth and all very good things.
claims: Mercy frees from misery; goodness creates and governs.

pl-l4d46c4-d1e131.summary: Adds Augustine: the heavens do not need mercy, where there is no misery; on earth man's misery abounds and the Lord's mercy superabounds; but all need the Lord, happy and wretched, since without him the wretched is not raised and the happy not ruled.
claims: All creatures need God's rule; only the wretched need mercy.

pl-l4d46c4-d1e140.summary: Adds: mercy is toward the wretched, goodness toward all.
claims: Mercy is toward the wretched, goodness toward all.

pl-l4d46c4-d1e146.summary: Notes that mercy is sometimes taken broadly as goodness.

pl-l4d46c4.summary: Scripture attributes some works to mercy, some to justice, some to goodness; mercy and justice are clear, goodness and mercy less so. Augustine: works proper to mercy free from misery, cleansing from sins; to goodness belong also the making and governing of natural things; the heavens need no mercy, having no misery, but need God's rule; mercy is toward the wretched, goodness toward all, though mercy is sometimes taken broadly as goodness.
claims: Goodness extends to creating and governing all things.
Mercy is toward the wretched, goodness toward all.
